title: Enterprise Banking Private Deployment: Workshop Notes, Scope & Costing Draft
body:
Context:
- Customer: regional enterprise bank (legal entity redacted in early draft). Risk/compliance-heavy workload: customer data cannot leave VPC.
- Objective: validate Redwood Private on customer ASH (Air-gapped Single Host) and planned VPC deployment for latency-sensitive customer service assistant and document ingestion pipeline.
- Ask from GTM/AE: output a deployable scope + high-level fixed-cost SOW option and a T&M alternative, plus a 2-day technical workshop agenda for infra + security stakeholders.

Workshop summary (session on 2025-08-04):
- Attendees: customer infra lead, customer security architect, product manager, Redwood SEs (Aisha, Rafa), infra engineer (Mina).
- Format: 2 half-day sessions. Day 1: architecture review and security/governance. Day 2: hands-on deploy checklist, baseline performance run.
- Key outcomes: customer will provision a staging subnet with VPN access and sample S3-equivalent store (MinIO). They confirmed FIPS KMS requirement and HSM for key wrapping.
- Unresolved: exact HSM vendor (Thales vs. customer-managed AWS CloudHSM). Need confirm by 2025-08-13.

Proposed engagement options (deliverables + timing):
Option A — Fixed-price SOW (recommended for procurement):
  - Discovery & compliance gap analysis (2 weeks): inventory of network restrictions, data-flow diagram, regulatory checks.
  - Private deployment setup (3 engineers, 1 week onsite/remote coordinate + remote 2 weeks): image packaging, air-gapped installer validation, KMS/HSM integration, registry mirroring.
  - Performance validation & tuning (2 weeks): run 3 benchmark scenarios (chat 25 req/s at 8k context; embedding pipeline 40 req/s batch; long-form generation 5 req/s), produce optimization plan.
  - Knowledge transfer & runbook (1 week): operator runbook, disaster recovery runbook, handoff workshop.
  - Total timeline: ~6–8 weeks from kickoff.
  - Suggested fixed price (draft): $220k – includes travel for up to 2 onsite days, 3 SEs (60 person-days), and test infra costs.

Option B — Time & Materials (flexible, lower upfront):
  - Bill at standard SE rate (internal reference rate: $1,600/day) + project manager $1,800/day. Estimate 60–90 days.
  - Customer prefers fixed for procurement simplicity; they asked for both.

Breakdown & assumptions used for costing:
- SE effort estimate: discovery 4pd, packaging 8pd, installer validation 8pd, KMS/HSM 6pd, perf validation 10pd, docs/hand-off 4pd. Contingency 20%.
- Travel: included for two onsite travel days (Rafa + Aisha) for knowledge transfer / exec alignment.
- Test infra: assume Redwood-managed test cluster in customer VPC for up to 2 weeks; any extended cloud charges billed separately.
- Third-party licenses: if customer requires specific vendor components (e.g., FIPS-enabled HSM) procurement by customer unless otherwise negotiated.

Technical scope (short form):
- Platform image prep: containerized runtime images, signed artifacts mirrored to customer registry.
- Installer: air-gapped tarball + helm manifests for disconnected k8s. Include manifest variables for node sizing and GPU labeling.
- KMS/HSM: support for AWS KMS + CloudHSM or Thales; wrap keys with HSM; operator-level key rotation documented.
- Network: require NAT egress only for initial artifact bootstrap OR pre-seed registry; production run may be fully offline. VPN for telemetry control-plane endpoints if requested.
- Observability: minimal on-prem metrics + optional forwarding to Redwood Console (customer approval required).
- Security controls: RBAC mappings, audit logging to customer SIEM, encrypted at-rest for model caches and KV cache.

Sizing / perf assumptions used in estimate:
- Workload profile provided: 60% chat-style short-turn (avg 120 tokens), 30% embeddings (batch up to 64), 10% long-form (avg 2,400 tokens).
- Baseline target: 99th percentile latency <= 250ms for short-turn; throughput target 50 tokens/sec per GPU for long-form when batched.
- Recommended baseline HW: 4x A100 40GB or 6x H100-80GB (preferred for large long-form), 128GB RAM per node, 2x NVMe cache 2TB.
- Estimated GPU-hours for benchmarks: 240 GPU-hours. Included in fixed-cost but note if extended benchmarking requested charges apply.

Acceptance criteria (delivery):
- Successful deployment of Redwood Private image into customer staging with documented commands.
- End-to-end test run: ingestion -> vector store -> query -> response validated against sample prompts (pass/fail tests attached).
- Performance report: measured P50/P95/P99 for the three benchmark scenarios and tuning actions performed.
- Handoff: runbook + 2-hour live ops training.

Risks & mitigation:
- HSM vendor delays: mitigate by offering AWS CloudHSM fallback or using a temporarily customer-managed KMS with strict rotation and encryption at rest.
- Network restrictions blocking bootstrap: pre-seed registries and images; bring-your-own USB transfer plan in worst-case. Plan a 3-day contingency window.
- Model licensing complications (customer wants to bring custom LLM weights): require EULA review; model file size may affect bundle approach — factor +2 days for large models.

Unresolved pricing questions for legal/finance:
- Treatment of test infra cloud charges in fixed-price SOW (absorbed vs. pass-through). Proposed approach: pass-through with cap $5k unless otherwise approved.
- VAT/import duties on physical media for air-gapped installs (if needed).

Workshop agenda (draft 2-day):
Day 1 — Governance, Security & Architecture (3 hours)
  - Introductions + success metrics (15m)
  - Data flow & compliance mapping (45m)
  - KMS/HSM options & crypto requirements (45m)
  - Network topology / registry mirroring options (30m)
  - Q&A & open items (45m)

Day 2 — Hands-on deployment checklist & perf plan (3.5 hours)
  - Installer walkthrough + required artifacts list (40m)
  - Demo: staging deploy (30m)
  - Benchmark plan & sample scripts (40m)
  - Ops/runbook draft review (40m)
  - Next steps + signoffs (20m)

Notes & action items (owner / due):
- Customer to confirm HSM vendor selection by 2025-08-13 (owner: customer sec architect).
- SEs to prepare air-gap packaging checklist and pre-seed registry instructions by 2025-08-08 (owner: Aisha).
- Legal to provide draft SOW template for fixed-price offering with pass-through infra cap by 2025-08-15 (owner: Solutions-eng legal liaison).
- Perf scripts (initial) to be uploaded to github repo under proposal branch (Rafa) by 2025-08-09. Link: github.com/redwood-inference/private-deploy-helm/tree/proposal-2025

Recommendations (SE opinion):
- Customer should choose fixed-price SOW for procurement simplicity and defined acceptance criteria; include a 10% contingency reserve in the budget.
- Recommend H100-class machines if customer expects a non-trivial long-form generation load in year 1; if cost constrained, tier to A100 with clear QC targets.
- Include a 12-month optional support & maintenance package priced annually (example: $75k/yr for 24×7 response SLOs and patch management).

Next steps (for AE / Solutions lead):
1) Turn this draft into a two-page SOW summary for procurement (deliverable due 2025-08-12).
2) Prepare itemized fixed-price SOW cost sheet (line items: SE days, travel, test infra cap, contingencies, support add-on).
3) Schedule follow-up call with customer to confirm HSM choice and procurement timeline (target week of 2025-08-18).

Appendix (quick refs):
- Quick checklist for air-gapped installer: signed image tarball, sha256 manifest, customer registry mirroring guide, env var template, offline license token.
- Benchmark scenarios listed and expected success metrics (attached as small csv in repo).

Draft status: internal working draft; do not share externally without legal/AE signoff.
